findings.F1: The coin's own 10-day return scaled by its 20-day daily volatility predicts its excess return over the next 10 days. On the non-overlapping 10-day grid, the pooled slope of the standardised excess return on it is 0.092 with t 3.58 over 1403 independent cases. That is stronger than the tested volume-ratio slope measured the same way, 0.045 with t 1.75 over 1403 cases.
findings.F2: The continuation is specific to a 10-day lookback and a 10-day horizon, and it is monotonic at the top end.
findings.F3: The momentum effect is absent in calm conditions. In the lowest 20-day-volatility tercile the 10-day-return slope is 0.044 (t 1.14, n 468), against 0.124 (t 2.88, n 467) in the middle tercile and 0.103 (t 1.99, n 468) in the high tercile. It is positive for 5 of 6 coins (ZEC t 2.70, LTC -0.45), but it changes sign by year (2020 t 3.21, 2018 t -1.34).
findings.F4: The tested volume surge works only when the coin is calm. Its slope is 0.180 (t 3.04, n 468) in the lowest 20-day-volatility tercile, 0.095 (t 1.44) in the middle and -0.014 (t -0.19) in the high tercile. In the calm tercile it is positive for 5 of 6 coins (XRP t 2.27, ETH -0.17), but by year it rests largely on 2024 (t 3.93, n 92).
findings.F5: The book's best days come after the coin had already run up. On the top 1 % of book days (174 days) the coin's prior 10-day return averaged +9.1 %, against +2.8 % before the worst 1 % and +1.2 % over all 17380 coin-days. On those best days the coin itself moved +16.4 % on the day.
findings.F6: The brief's close-location effect does not appear.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 10-day return relative to its own recent daily volatility, the more the coin keeps moving the same way over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans with a coin's volatility-adjusted 10-day move for the next 10 days, more so the larger the move, and refuses trades against it.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled ten-day continuation

ideas.idea: When a coin's 20-day volatility is low, the heavier its volume on a day relative to its prior 20-day average, the more it rises over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: In a calm coin, a trader leans long for 10 days after a volume surge, more so the larger the surge, and refuses shorts.
ideas.name: calm-market volume surge rise

ideas.idea: When a coin's 20-day volatility is middling to high, the larger its 10-day return, the more it keeps rising over the next 10 days, and the larger its 10-day fall, the more it keeps falling.
ideas.consequence: Once a coin is moving actively, a trader follows its 10-day move for the next 10 days, more so the larger the move, and refuses to fade it.
ideas.name: active-market ten-day momentum
